heuristics.rule: Use NOC 60010 (Corporate sales managers) as the official Canadian classification for Product Manager roles
heuristics.condition: When classifying a Product Manager role for immigration, labour market, or wage benchmark purposes in Canada
heuristics.action: Reference NOC 60010 and its associated wage bands as the governing classification
heuristics.because: NOC 60010 is the official Government of Canada classification that encompasses Product Managers; using an alternate NOC code would misrepresent the occupational classification
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Canada Job Bank NOC 60010 — Corporate sales managers; https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/marketreport/wages-occupation/26656/ca

heuristics.rule: Alberta median hourly wage ($65.00/hr) exceeds Ontario median ($60.10/hr) for NOC 60010
heuristics.condition: When comparing provincial PM wage benchmarks for compensation negotiation or labour market impact assessment
heuristics.action: Treat Alberta as the highest-median province for PM wages, not Ontario or BC
heuristics.because: Labour Force Survey data (2023–2024) places Alberta median at $65.00/hr vs. Ontario at $60.10/hr and BC at $55.65/hr
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Canada Job Bank — Provincial wage data, NOC 60010, reference period 2023–2024

heuristics.rule: Toronto CMA high wage ceiling ($147.06/hr, ~$306,000 CAD/yr) is the highest reported regional ceiling for PM wages in Canada
heuristics.condition: When determining maximum achievable PM compensation within Canada without relocating to the US
heuristics.action: Treat $147.06/hr (~$306K CAD/yr) as the Canadian PM compensation ceiling, applicable only in the Toronto CMA
heuristics.because: Job Bank regional data identifies this as the top-of-market figure for senior/principal PMs at FAANG Canada offices and major financial institutions in Toronto
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Canada Job Bank — Toronto CMA regional data, NOC 60010; https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/marketreport/wages-occupation/26656/geo9219

heuristics.rule: Annual salary estimates in the Labour Force Survey are calculated using 2,080 hours/year (40 hrs/week × 52 weeks)
heuristics.condition: When converting Job Bank hourly wage data to annual salary figures
heuristics.action: Apply 2,080-hour multiplier to hourly figures; note that bonuses, overtime, and equity are not captured
heuristics.because: LFS wage data does not include equity (RSUs, options), overtime, or bonus compensation; actual total comp may materially differ
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Government of Canada Job Bank data notes, NOC 60010

decision_factors.why_it_matters: PM wages vary materially by province; Alberta median ($65.00/hr) exceeds BC median ($55.65/hr) by ~17%, and Ontario high ceiling ($132.57/hr) far exceeds BC high ($89.25/hr)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare the applicable provincial wage band from Job Bank NOC 60010 provincial table; reference period 2023–2024

decision_factors.why_it_matters: 98.9% of product managers nationally receive at least one non-wage benefit (pension, insurance, leave entitlements); near-universal benefit coverage is a structural feature of Canadian PM employment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether employer provides at least one non-wage benefit; 98.9% national rate and 99.2% Ontario rate and 100% BC rate establish the norm

decision_factors.factor: Employer type and sector (FAANG Canada, fintech, banking, energy)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The high wage ceiling in Toronto ($147.06/hr) is driven specifically by FAANG Canada offices (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) and large Canadian fintech/banking tech employers (RBC, TD, Shopify); BC's lower ceiling reflects fewer Principal/Staff PM seats
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether employer is a FAANG Canada office, major Canadian financial institution, or energy-sector employer to determine applicable wage band ceiling

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Equity at FAANG Canada offices and tech unicorns (Shopify) can add CAD $20,000–$100,000+ to total comp above LFS wage figures, which do not capture equity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether employer offers RSU or option grants; LFS wage data will understate total comp by $20K–$100K+ at qualifying employers

decision_factors.factor: Regional classification within province (CMA vs. non-CMA)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Toronto CMA high wage ($147.06/hr) exceeds provincial Ontario high ($132.57/hr); Vancouver Lower Mainland median ($57.04/hr) exceeds BC provincial median ($55.65/hr)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use region-specific Job Bank data (e.g., Toronto CMA, Lower Mainland–Southwest) rather than provincial averages when the role is in a major urban centre

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Remaining in Canada rather than relocating to the US for a Senior PM role
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: National median is ~$125K CAD, materially below equivalent US Senior PM roles (USD $180K–$250K base); the Canadian compensation ceiling of ~$306K CAD (~$147/hr in Toronto) is the hard upper limit without US relocation
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Senior and Principal PMs at or near the top of the Canadian market who are evaluating US relocation decisions

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a PM role in British Columbia (Vancouver) over Ontario (Toronto)
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: BC provincial high wage ceiling is $89.25/hr vs. $132.57/hr in Ontario — a 48% lower ceiling — despite Vancouver being a recognized major tech hub; fewer Principal/Staff PM seats and lower concentration of top-paying employers constrains long-term comp growth in BC
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Senior PMs and Principal PMs choosing between Vancouver and Toronto job markets

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on LFS hourly wage data as a complete picture of PM total compensation
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: LFS data excludes equity (RSUs, options), bonuses, and overtime; at FAANG Canada offices and Shopify, equity alone can add CAD $20,000–$100,000+ annually, meaning stated wage figures systematically understate total comp at top employers
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs benchmarking offers at FAANG Canada, Shopify, or tech unicorns using Job Bank data alone

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Using NOC 60010 wage data as a precise PM-specific benchmark
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: NOC 60010 (Corporate sales managers) is broader than the tech-specific PM role; the classification includes non-tech sales managers, which may dilute the wage data and cause it to understate or misrepresent wages for tech PMs specifically
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Tech PMs using Job Bank data for offer negotiation or immigration wage compliance purposes

failure_patterns.pattern: Using national median ($125K CAD) as the benchmark for a Toronto-based senior PM offer evaluation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: National LFS data pools all provinces and all employer types under NOC 60010; Toronto CMA data shows a median of $59.55/hr (~$124K) but a high of $147.06/hr (~$306K), meaning the national median is not representative of top-market Toronto offers
failure_patterns.consequence: Systematic undervaluation of compensation expectations for senior/principal PM roles at FAANG Canada or major financial institutions in Toronto
warning_signs: Evaluating a Toronto FAANG PM offer against the $125K CAD national median
Not distinguishing between Toronto CMA regional data and national or provincial data

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming BC (Vancouver) and Ontario (Toronto) have comparable PM compensation ceilings because both are major tech hubs
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: BC provincial high is $89.25/hr vs. Ontario provincial high of $132.57/hr; Toronto CMA high is $147.06/hr — a gap of over 60% at the ceiling
failure_patterns.consequence: Materially incorrect compensation benchmarking for senior PM roles in Vancouver relative to Toronto
warning_signs: Treating Vancouver and Toronto as interchangeable PM markets for compensation purposes
Using BC provincial wage data to evaluate a Toronto offer or vice versa

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the PM role located in the Toronto CMA, another Ontario region, or a different province?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which wage band applies — Toronto CMA data (high: $147.06/hr), Ontario provincial data (high: $132.57/hr), or another province's data
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Toronto CMA: use Job Bank Toronto CMA data (https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/marketreport/wages-occupation/26656/geo9219) as the applicable benchmark
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If outside Toronto CMA: identify the correct provincial or regional wage table from Job Bank NOC 60010 data

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the employer a FAANG Canada office, major Canadian financial institution (RBC, TD), or tech unicorn (Shopify)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the role is likely to include equity (RSUs, options) of CAD $20,000–$100,000+ that is not captured in LFS wage data
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Total compensation will materially exceed LFS wage figures; equity must be assessed separately
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: LFS wage data is more likely to represent total cash comp accurately, though bonuses may still not be captured

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the employer provide at least one non-wage benefit (pension, insurance, leave entitlements)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the offer meets the near-universal Canadian market norm (98.9% nationally, 99.2% in Ontario, 100% in BC)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Offer is consistent with market standard for non-wage benefits
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Offer is below market norm; absence of any non-wage benefit is atypical for fewer than 1.1% of Canadian PM roles nationally

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the PM role being classified under NOC 60010 for immigration or labour market purposes?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the correct official classification is being applied; NOC 60010 is broader than tech-specific PM and includes corporate sales managers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm that the wage offered meets the applicable NOC 60010 wage band for the region; note the broader classification may affect LMIA or Express Entry assessments
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Identify which NOC code is being used and verify it is appropriate for the specific role

industry_realities.common_belief: Vancouver (BC) and Toronto (Ontario) offer comparable PM compensation ceilings because both are major Canadian tech hubs
industry_realities.actual_reality: Ontario provincial high is $132.57/hr and Toronto CMA high is $147.06/hr; BC provincial high is $89.25/hr — a ceiling gap of approximately 48–65% in favour of Toronto
industry_realities.implication: Senior PMs and Principal PMs maximizing Canadian compensation should prioritize Toronto over Vancouver; BC's lower ceiling reflects fewer Principal/Staff PM seats and lower concentration of top-paying employers

industry_realities.common_belief: Alberta has a smaller tech sector than Ontario or BC, so PM wages there are lower
industry_realities.actual_reality: Alberta provincial median is $65.00/hr (~$135,200 CAD/yr), the highest provincial median in Canada, exceeding Ontario ($60.10/hr) and BC ($55.65/hr)
industry_realities.implication: Alberta median PM wages are the highest in Canada despite a smaller tech sector, driven by energy-sector PM roles and employer mix in Calgary/Edmonton

industry_realities.common_belief: Job Bank wage data captures total PM compensation
industry_realities.actual_reality: LFS wage data excludes equity (RSUs, options), bonuses, and overtime; at FAANG Canada offices and Shopify, equity alone can add CAD $20,000–$100,000+ annually above reported figures
industry_realities.implication: Job Bank wage data systematically understates total comp at top Canadian tech employers; equity must be assessed through separate sources

industry_realities.common_belief: NOC 60010 is a precise classification for tech Product Managers
industry_realities.actual_reality: NOC 60010 is formally titled 'Corporate sales managers' and is broader than the tech-specific PM usage; it is the official classification that encompasses Product Managers but includes non-tech roles
industry_realities.implication: Wage data under NOC 60010 may be diluted by non-tech corporate sales manager salaries; users should account for this when benchmarking tech PM compensation specifically

industry_realities.common_belief: The Canadian PM compensation ceiling is comparable to mid-tier US tech PM salaries
industry_realities.actual_reality: The Canadian PM ceiling is ~$306K CAD/yr (Toronto CMA high, $147.06/hr); equivalent US Senior PM roles pay USD $180K–$250K base, with total comp potentially higher; the source states the Canadian median is 'materially below' US equivalents
industry_realities.implication: PMs prioritizing maximum compensation must account for the structural US-Canada compensation gap when making relocation decisions
